# CI: the suite's lanes on every pull request, on every push to main and every night, and a
# check that the package installs clean and that its docs run as written.
#
# The lanes are the four pyproject.toml names, mark for mark, and release.yml runs the same
# ones on a tag, so CI and a release cannot drift apart.
#
# - pull-request: on every pull request, push and night, on Python 3.11, the oldest the package
#   declares: the pull-request lane, ruff check src tests and mypy --strict. Nothing skips it.
# - math: the statistics' slow checks against their references. Every night and on every push
#   to main; on a pull request only when .github/lanes/math_lane.py says the pull request could
#   have moved a statistic (the statistics code, a test of the math suite, the declared
#   dependencies, or a numpy, scipy, pandas or lifelines other than the lanes were green with).
# - full: on main and every night, never on a pull request: the pull-request lane and the slow
#   lane on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, with ruff and mypy --strict on each.
# - lane-j: on main and every night, never on a pull request: the one job that reads the
#   package index for other tools. It installs the real DeepEval and Ragas and runs the tests
#   that run them, and the test that the built wheel brings the Prove it pins.
# - clean-install: builds the source archive and the wheel from the commit; installs one of
#   them with plain pip into a fresh environment (the wheel in one cell, the source archive in
#   the other); moves to an empty folder with a home of its own; checks that the package
#   imported is the installed one; then, with every connection but to this machine refused,
#   runs every marked block of the README and the docs through tools/docs_check.py. Every
#   block the docs check skipped is listed in the job's summary.
#
# Left for the CI setup session to choose, and written here only so the file runs: the runner
# of each job and the systems the full job covers (macos-latest below, where the lanes were
# last made green), how the jobs are cut into shards, how the socket guard is made, and
# whether clean-install runs on every pull request.
#
# The workflow reads the repository and nothing else. It holds no secret and asks for no
# token. Every action is pinned to a full commit SHA. CI is unset for every pytest line: Trace
# reads CI as a reason to print plain text, and the tests pin what it prints without it.

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * *"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  BUILD_VERSION: "1.6.1"
  PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK: "1"
  OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS: "1"

jobs:
  pull-request:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Environment
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install --quiet -c .github/release/lanes-3.11.txt -e ".[dev]"
          .venv/bin/python --version
          .venv/bin/poisson-trace --version
      - name: Tasks' tokenizer file, which the three-tools recipe the lanes run needs
        run: .venv/bin/poisson-tasks doctor --fix --yes
      - name: Pull-request lane
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n auto -q -p no:cacheprovider -m "not math and not lane_j and not slow" tests
      - name: ruff
        run: .venv/bin/ruff check src tests
      - name: mypy --strict
        run: .venv/bin/mypy --strict

  math:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Environment
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install --quiet -e ".[dev]"
          .venv/bin/python -m pip freeze | grep -i -E "^(numpy|scipy|pandas|lifelines)=="
      # The rule is .github/lanes/math_lane.py's: the statistics code (src/poisson_trace/paired.py,
      # src/poisson_trace/survival.py, src/poisson_trace/stats), a test of the math suite, the
      # declared dependencies, or a resolved numpy, scipy, pandas or lifelines that moved.
      - name: Whether this event runs the math lane
        id: rule
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: .venv/bin/python .github/lanes/math_lane.py $BASE
      - name: Math lane
        if: steps.rule.outputs.run == 'true'
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n auto -q -p no:cacheprovider -m math tests

  full:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 180
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      # The versions the lanes were last green with are recorded for Python 3.11 and 3.12; on
      # a Python with no such file, pip resolves the newest versions the package allows.
      - name: Environment
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          constraints=".github/release/lanes-${{ matrix.python }}.txt"
          if [ -f "$constraints" ]; then
            .venv/bin/python -m pip install --quiet -c "$constraints" -e ".[dev]"
          else
            .venv/bin/python -m pip install --quiet -e ".[dev]"
          fi
          .venv/bin/python --version
      - name: Tasks' tokenizer file, which the three-tools recipe the lanes run needs
        run: .venv/bin/poisson-tasks doctor --fix --yes
      - name: Pull-request lane
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n auto -q -p no:cacheprovider -m "not math and not lane_j and not slow" tests
      - name: Slow lane
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n auto -q -p no:cacheprovider -m slow tests
      - name: ruff
        run: .venv/bin/ruff check src tests
      - name: mypy --strict
        run: .venv/bin/mypy --strict

  lane-j:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Environment
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install --quiet -c .github/release/lanes-3.12.txt -e ".[dev]"
      # The tests install the two tools themselves, each at the version it pins. This step
      # fails early and plainly when the package index cannot serve them, and warms pip's cache.
      - name: The real DeepEval and Ragas, from the package index
        run: |
          DEEPEVAL=$(sed -n 's/^DEEPEVAL = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' tests/ingest/test_deepeval_package.py)
          python -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet "deepeval==$DEEPEVAL" ragas
      - name: Lane J
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m lane_j tests

  clean-install:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        install: [wheel, sdist]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Build the source archive and the wheel from the commit
        run: |
          python -m pip install --quiet "build==$BUILD_VERSION"
          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/tree"
          git archive --format=tar HEAD | tar -x -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/tree"
          python -m build --outdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tree"
          ls -l "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist"
      - name: Install it with plain pip into a fresh environment
        run: |
          python -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean"
          if [ "${{ matrix.install }}" = "wheel" ]; then
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet "$RUNNER_TEMP"/dist/*.whl
          else
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet "$RUNNER_TEMP"/dist/*.tar.gz
          fi
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip check
      # The three-tools recipe runs Poisson Tasks and the team's own pytest file. Neither Trace
      # nor Tasks brings pytest, so it is installed here, as the recipe's install line does.
      - name: Poisson Tasks at its pin, its tokenizer file and pytest, for the three-tools recipe
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet "poisson-tasks==0.4.2" pytest
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/poisson-tasks" doctor --fix --yes
      - name: An empty folder, a home of its own, and the package that was installed
        run: |
          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/empty" "$RUNNER_TEMP/home"
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/empty"
          export HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/home"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/poisson-trace" --version | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -c "import pathlib, sys, poisson_trace; where = pathlib.Path(poisson_trace.__file__).resolve(); env = pathlib.Path(sys.prefix).resolve(); assert env in where.parents, (where, env); print(where)"
      # From here on every Python refuses a connection to any address that is not this
      # machine's, and writes it down: the guard is sitecustomize.py in a folder on PYTHONPATH.
      - name: Socket guard, so that no connection leaves this machine
        run: |
          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/guard"
          cp .github/lanes/socket_guard.py "$RUNNER_TEMP/guard/sitecustomize.py"
          echo "PYTHONPATH=$RUNNER_TEMP/guard" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "POISSON_TRACE_REFUSED=$RUNNER_TEMP/refused.log" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Every marked block of the README and the docs, run as written
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/empty"
          export HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/home"
          export PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin:$PATH"
          python "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/tools/docs_check.py" --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Nothing reached for the network, and nothing was left in the empty folder
        run: |
          if [ -e "$RUNNER_TEMP/refused.log" ]; then cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/refused.log"; exit 1; fi
          test -z "$(ls -A "$RUNNER_TEMP/empty")"

# Release: a signed tag vX.Y.Z (or a pre-release such as v0.1.0a1) publishes that version to
# TestPyPI; starting this workflow by hand on that tag then publishes the same files to PyPI.
#
# This file is .github/workflows/release.yml, and PyPI's and TestPyPI's trusted publishers for
# poisson-trace name it by exactly that file name, release.yml, with the environment `pypi`.
#
# The repository is private on GitHub Team, where an environment cannot require a reviewer, so
# the approval is the hand start (ruled 2026-11-11): only a run started with "Run workflow" on
# the tag, the version typed in, reaches PyPI.
#
# On the tag (push):
# - check: the ref is a tag GitHub verified as signed; the tag, pyproject.toml, __version__ and
#   the CHANGELOG entry agree; no commit names an assistant.
# - build: the sdist and the wheel from the tagged tree (`git archive`, never the checkout);
#   twine's metadata check; every requirement one an index can serve, Prove pinned exactly; the
#   wheel holds the package alone, and neither file an absolute path or a key. Kept as `dist`.
# - lanes, on Python 3.12 and 3.11: pull-request, slow, math, ruff, mypy --strict.
# - lane-j, on Python 3.12 and 3.11: the built wheel installed into a clean environment brings
#   the Prove it pins and reads a store; and lane J's own clean-install test.
# - testpypi: uploads `dist` to TestPyPI by trusted publishing; testpypi-check then checks
#   TestPyPI serves those files byte for byte and that they install and run.
# By hand on the tag (workflow_dispatch, version typed in):
# - check, as above, and the version typed is the tag's.
# - pypi-ready: a run on this tag's push passed every job; its `dist` is the one TestPyPI
#   serves, byte for byte.
# - pypi: uploads that `dist` to PyPI by trusted publishing; pypi-check then checks PyPI
#   serves those files and that they install and run.
#
# Only testpypi and pypi may ask for an OIDC token, and only in the environment `pypi`. No
# password or API token is stored anywhere. Every action is pinned to a full commit SHA.

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Publish to PyPI: the version, as the tag names it without its v (0.1.0a1). Run on the tag, not on a branch."
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  BUILD_VERSION: "1.6.1"
  TWINE_VERSION: "7.0.0"
  PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK: "1"
  OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS: "1"

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Run on a tag GitHub verified as signed
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != tag ]; then
            echo "::error::run this workflow on a tag v*, not on $GITHUB_REF_TYPE $GITHUB_REF_NAME"; exit 1
          fi
          ref=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/ref/tags/$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --jq '.object.type + " " + .object.sha')
          if [ "${ref%% *}" != tag ]; then
            echo "::error::$GITHUB_REF_NAME is a lightweight tag; a release tag is made with git tag -s"; exit 1
          fi
          verified=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/tags/${ref#* }" --jq '.verification.verified, .verification.reason' | paste -sd' ' -)
          echo "tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME: verified, reason: $verified"
          if [ "${verified%% *}" != true ]; then
            echo "::error::GitHub does not verify the signature on $GITHUB_REF_NAME ($verified)"; exit 1
          fi
      - name: By hand, the version typed is the tag's
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          TYPED: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          if [ "v$TYPED" != "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" ]; then
            echo "::error::typed $TYPED; this run is on $GITHUB_REF_NAME"; exit 1
          fi
      - name: The tag, the version and the CHANGELOG agree
        run: python .github/release/release_check.py tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"
      - name: No commit names an assistant
        run: python .github/release/history.py

  build:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Build the sdist and the wheel from the tagged tree
        run: |
          python -m pip install --quiet "build==$BUILD_VERSION" "twine==$TWINE_VERSION"
          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/tree"
          git archive --format=tar HEAD | tar -x -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/tree"
          python -m build --outdir dist "$RUNNER_TEMP/tree"
          twine check --strict dist/*
          ls -l dist
          sha256sum dist/* | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Requirements an index can serve; nothing in the files that should not be
        run: python .github/release/release_check.py dist dist | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 90
          if-no-files-found: error

  lanes:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: check
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.12", "3.11"]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 180
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - name: Environment
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install --quiet -c ".github/release/lanes-${{ matrix.python }}.txt" -e ".[dev]"
          .venv/bin/python --version
      - name: Tasks' tokenizer file, which the three-tools recipe the lanes run needs
        run: .venv/bin/poisson-tasks doctor --fix --yes
      # CI is unset for the tests, as on the machines the lanes were made green on: Trace reads CI
      # as a reason to print plain, and the tests of the terminal look set it themselves.
      - name: Pull-request lane
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n auto -q -p no:cacheprovider -m "not math and not lane_j and not slow" tests
      - name: Slow lane
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n auto -q -p no:cacheprovider -m slow tests
      - name: Math lane
        run: env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n auto -q -p no:cacheprovider -m math tests
      - name: ruff
        run: .venv/bin/ruff check src tests
      - name: mypy --strict
        run: .venv/bin/mypy --strict

  lane-j:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: build
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.12", "3.11"]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
      - name: The built wheel, installed alone into a clean environment, brings its Prove and reads a store
        run: |
          python -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet dist/*.whl
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip check
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/poisson-trace" --version | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -c "import importlib.metadata as m; assert m.version('poisson-prove') == '0.1.3', m.version('poisson-prove')"
          NO_COLOR=1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/poisson-trace" fix-check "tau2-airline 2026-09-15 a" "tau2-airline 2026-09-15 b" \
            --store "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/tests/fixtures/tau2" --event unsolved --inputs all --max-mde 0.2 --json > fix-check.json
          python -c "import json; d = json.load(open('fix-check.json')); print(d['verdict'], '|', d['direction'], '| p', d['test']['p'])"
      - name: Lane J's clean-install test
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install --quiet -c ".github/release/lanes-${{ matrix.python }}.txt" -e ".[dev]"
          env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m lane_j \
            "tests/test_prove_pin.py::test_pin_1_a_clean_install_of_the_wheel_brings_the_recorded_prove"

  testpypi:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: [build, lanes, lane-j]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://test.pypi.org/project/poisson-trace/
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
      - name: Publish to TestPyPI
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2
        with:
          repository-url: https://test.pypi.org/legacy/
          # a re-run after a later job failed finds the files there; testpypi-check still
          # holds TestPyPI's files to these, byte for byte
          skip-existing: true

  testpypi-check:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: testpypi
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
      - name: TestPyPI serves these files, and they install and run
        run: |
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          python .github/release/release_check.py index testpypi dist "$version" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          # Trace from TestPyPI alone; what it requires from PyPI
          python -m pip download --quiet --no-deps --only-binary :all: --dest "$RUNNER_TEMP/from-test" \
            --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ "poisson-trace==$version"
          python -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet "$RUNNER_TEMP"/from-test/*.whl
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/poisson-trace" --version | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  pypi-ready:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      run-id: ${{ steps.run.outputs.id }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - id: run
        name: A run on this tag's push passed every job
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          id=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/release.yml/runs?event=push&head_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&status=success&per_page=1" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
          if [ -z "$id" ]; then
            echo "::error::no successful release run on the push of $GITHUB_REF_NAME ($GITHUB_SHA); PyPI waits for one"; exit 1
          fi
          echo "id=$id" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "the tag's run: $GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$id" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
          run-id: ${{ steps.run.outputs.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: That run's files are the ones TestPyPI serves
        run: python .github/release/release_check.py index testpypi dist "${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  pypi:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    needs: pypi-ready
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/project/poisson-trace/
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
          run-id: ${{ needs.pypi-ready.outputs.run-id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Publish to PyPI
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2

  pypi-check:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    needs: [pypi-ready, pypi]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
          run-id: ${{ needs.pypi-ready.outputs.run-id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: PyPI serves these files, and they install and run
        run: |
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          python .github/release/release_check.py index pypi dist "$version" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          python -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet "poisson-trace==$version"
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$RUNNER_TEMP/clean/bin/poisson-trace" --version | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# Contributing to Poisson Trace

This page is for someone changing Trace itself: how to get a working copy, how to run the
suite, and the rules a change is held to. If you only want to use Trace, the
[README](README.md) is the place to start.

## A working copy

Trace needs Python 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13. The suite is run on two of them before a change is
merged: Python 3.11, the oldest the package declares, and Python 3.12. Make an environment
for each:

<!-- skip reason="a contributor's commands: shown here, and not run by the docs check" -->
```
git clone https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace
cd trace
python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e '.[dev]'
python3.11 -m venv .venv311 && .venv311/bin/pip install -e '.[dev]'
.venv/bin/poisson-trace --version
```

The development install also brings Poisson Tasks, which one recipe the suite runs needs
(`docs/recipes/with-tasks-and-prove.md`). Tasks needs a tokenizer file it does not ship. Fetch
it once in each environment, or that recipe's tests fail at its first command:
`.venv/bin/poisson-tasks doctor --fix --yes`, and the same with `.venv311`.

The last line prints the version of Trace, of Prove and of Python. Prove is the
`poisson-prove` package, which Trace reads stored runs through. `pyproject.toml` pins it to
one exact version, and `pip` brings it.

## The suite

The tests are in four lanes, told apart by marks that `pyproject.toml` names. Each line below
is one lane, and `-n 10` runs it on ten workers:

<!-- skip reason="a contributor's commands: shown here, and not run by the docs check" -->
```
env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n 10 -m "not math and not lane_j and not slow" tests
env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n 10 -m slow tests
env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n 10 -m math tests
env -u CI .venv/bin/python -m pytest -m lane_j tests
```

- The first is the pull-request lane: everything that is quick. It runs on every pull request.
- `-m slow` holds the long form of tests whose short form is in the pull-request lane: every
  case of a set where the quick lane runs a few.
- `-m math` holds the statistics' slow checks against their references. Run it when you change
  `src/poisson_trace/paired.py`, `survival.py` or anything under `src/poisson_trace/stats`, or
  when numpy, scipy, pandas or lifelines move.
- `-m lane_j` is the one lane that reaches the package index: it installs the real DeepEval
  and Ragas and runs them. It is left out unless you ask for it.

`env -u CI` matters: Trace reads `CI` as a reason to print plain text, and the tests pin what
it prints without it.

Apart from `-m lane_j`, the suite makes no network call and no paid call, and reads no key.
The readers for LangSmith, Braintrust and Weave are tested against answers those services
gave once, kept under `tests/fixtures/ingest/`.

Then the linter and the type checker, on both Pythons, each with a cache of its own so that
one Python's cache is never read by the other:

<!-- skip reason="a contributor's commands: shown here, and not run by the docs check" -->
```
.venv/bin/ruff check src tests
.venv/bin/mypy --strict --cache-dir .mypy_cache_312
.venv311/bin/ruff check src tests
.venv311/bin/mypy --strict --cache-dir .mypy_cache_311
```

## The docs are tested too

Every command a page shows is run, and what the page says it printed is held to what it
printed. `tools/docs_check.py` does it, with whatever `poisson-trace` is first on your `PATH`:

<!-- skip reason="a contributor's commands: shown here, and not run by the docs check" -->
```
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python tools/docs_check.py
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python tools/docs_check.py docs/recipes/first-look.md
```

With no page it checks the README, this page and every page under `docs/` but the two
standards. A page marks each block with a comment on the line above it: `<!-- command -->`
for a block to run, `<!-- output exit=0 -->` for the whole of what it printed,
`<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->` for a run of its lines, and `<!-- skip reason="..." -->` for a block
that is shown and not run. The opening of `tools/docs_check.py` has the whole list. When you
change what a command prints, run the check and update the pages it names.

A page under `docs/` is written for a reader who has never seen Trace: plain words, every
number with its unit, and every claim shown by a command that runs. The README's blocks are
each a block of a recipe under `docs/recipes/`, so change the recipe and the README together.

## Frozen tests

Most test files are frozen: they were written and agreed before the code they test, and they
do not change to make a build pass. Each group of them has a guard, a file named
`test_*_frozen.py`, that holds the SHA-256 digest of every file in the group and fails when
one is edited.

A frozen test changes only when its owner rules that it should. The change goes in a commit
of its own, with the guard's line for that file moved in the same commit, and the commit says
which ruling it carries out. If a frozen test seems wrong, stop and ask: do not edit it, and
do not add a test that says the opposite.

## Fixtures

The files under `tests/fixtures/` are real: runs that Prove stored, and result files that
each tool wrote. None is written by hand. `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md` says where each came
from and how it was made, and `tests/fixtures/SHA256SUMS` holds the digest of each:

<!-- skip reason="a contributor's commands: shown here, and not run by the docs check" -->
```
cd tests/fixtures && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

A new reader needs a real export of its tool among the fixtures before its page may name the
tool, and a line in both files.

## The two standards

`docs/cli-look.md` says how every Poisson Labs command prints: the verdict line, the exit
codes, the colours, the plain form. `docs/repo-hygiene.md` says how a repository is kept.
Both are copies of the lab's own files, kept byte for byte, and a test holds them to that.
Do not edit them here.

## Commits and releases

Sign your commits. Keep a commit to one thing, and say in its message what changed for a
user. `CHANGELOG.md` gets a line for every change a user can see.

A release is a signed tag: `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds the package from the tag,
runs the lanes above on Python 3.11 and 3.12, and publishes. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs
the same lanes on pull requests and on `main`.

# Poisson Trace

Where in the workflow do your agent's runs die, and did your change make them fail less?

Trace answers both from results you already have: in LangSmith, Braintrust or Weave, in the
files your evaluation tool wrote, or in runs stored by
[Prove](https://github.com/poisson-labs/prove). It tells you:

- **where runs die**: at which step of the workflow, and at which kind of step, such as a
  model call or a tool call;
- **which inputs got worse** and **which kinds of failure grew**, between an old version and
  a new one;
- **whether it is real or noise**: one of *different*, *no significant difference* and
  *too small to tell*, and under the last, how many more tries would settle it.

    pip install poisson-trace
    poisson-trace init
    poisson-trace fix-check previous latest --inputs all --max-mde 0.2

- `poisson-trace init` finds the results in your folder, asks which outcomes count as a
  failure, and writes `trace.toml`. It runs nothing.
- `poisson-trace fix-check previous latest` compares your two newest runs, the old version
  beside the new one. `--inputs all` takes every input both runs hold, and `--max-mde 0.2`
  asks that the check be able to see a drop of 20 points in the share of tries that fail.
- `poisson-trace where latest` shows where the tries of the newest run die.
- `poisson-trace import` reads in results another tool holds: an experiment in LangSmith,
  Braintrust or Weave by its address, or a result file.
- `poisson-trace` on its own opens the terminal app: your runs, a comparison, a fix check and
  the verdict, a screen each.
- `poisson-trace init --agent` writes a setup file that your own coding agent follows to set
  Trace up, for you to review.

Python 3.11 to 3.13 on macOS and Linux. Trace runs nothing, captures nothing and sends nothing.

---

## Install

<!-- skip reason="installs from the package index, which the docs check does not reach" -->
```
pip install poisson-trace
```

That one line is all Trace needs. It brings Prove, the `poisson-prove` package that Trace
reads stored runs through, at the one exact version Trace reads. `poisson-trace --version`
prints the versions of Trace, Prove and Python, and `poisson-trace doctor` says whether the
setup is ready.

The examples on this page, and on every page under `docs/`, read example files that are in
the repository and not in the installed package. To run them as written, work in a clone of
the repository:

<!-- skip reason="fetches the repository, which the docs check does not reach" -->
```
git clone https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace
cd trace
```

Every command shown on these pages is run, and what a page says it printed is checked
against what it printed, each time the pages change.

## This is a pre-release

The package on PyPI today is Poisson Trace `0.1.0a1`, a pre-release, and this section stands
only until 0.1.0 is released. pip takes a pre-release only when you name its version. The
plain line above still gets `0.0.1`, a placeholder that does not run. Name the version:

<!-- skip reason="installs from the package index, which the docs check does not reach" -->
```
python3 -m venv trace-env
. trace-env/bin/activate
pip install poisson-trace==0.1.0a1
```

`poisson-trace --version` then prints the version it installed.

Trace needs Python 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13, and the `python3` that macOS ships is older. If
`python3 --version` prints a version below Python 3.11, type `python3.11`, `python3.12` or
`python3.13` in the first line, whichever your machine has.

The repository is private for now, so a link on this page to github.com/poisson-labs/trace
may not open for you. Every page it names is in the source archive, which is on PyPI beside
the package. Fetch it and work inside it in place of a clone:

<!-- skip reason="fetches from the package index, which the docs check does not reach" -->
```
pip download --no-deps --no-binary poisson-trace poisson-trace==0.1.0a1
tar -xzf poisson_trace-0.1.0a1.tar.gz
cd poisson_trace-0.1.0a1
```

Commands, flags and what they print may still change before 0.1.0. Send problems to
work@poissonlabs.ai, with the command you typed, what it printed, and what
`poisson-trace --version` prints.

## What a first run looks like

Five words come up on every page. A try is one attempt of your agent at one task. A run is
one stored sweep: every try of one version of your agent, kept together. A store is the
folder that holds runs. An input is one thing the agent was asked to do, and a run usually
tries each input more than once. A case is what an evaluation tool calls an input: a test
case, a dataset row, a question. An event is an outcome that counts as a failure, and you say
which outcomes those are.

### On runs Prove stored

`poisson-trace init` looks for results under the folder you run it in. Here that folder holds
two recordings of a customer-service agent demo, which Prove stored:

<!-- command -->
```
mkdir -p my-agent && cp -R tests/fixtures/cs my-agent/prove-runs
cd my-agent && poisson-trace init --yes
```

It says what it found:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
  found 1 store:
    1) prove-runs                2 runs · cs_agents · newest 2026-09-25
Using prove-runs, the store found.
```

and what it did:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  wrote trace.toml: store prove-runs (2 runs), failures app_error, forbidden_action, unresolved, max_turns
  names    2 runs, named from their manifests (cs_agents 2026-09-25 b, cs_agents 2026-09-25 a); none named by you yet: poisson-trace name RUN "a name"
  prove    poisson-prove is installed at the version Trace reads
```

`trace.toml` now names the store and the failures, so the commands after it need no flags.
`runs` lists what the store holds:

<!-- command -->
```
cd my-agent && poisson-trace runs
```

<!-- output exit=0 -->
```
ok  2 runs in prove-runs (newest first); 0 named by you, 2 named from their manifests

  #  name                    rows  failed  traces  started           status
  1  cs_agents 2026-09-25 b    24       7  yes     2026-09-25 23:54  complete
  2  cs_agents 2026-09-25 a    24       7  yes     2026-09-25 23:46  complete

next: poisson-trace where "cs_agents 2026-09-25 b"
```

and `where` reads the newest run:

<!-- command -->
```
cd my-agent && poisson-trace where latest
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  7 of 21 tries failed; their last steps: 4 at a model call and 3 at an agent step (not necessarily the cause)
```

The report puts every try on one clock, the step it had reached, and gives the share of
tries that had not failed by each step where one did:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## Share not yet failed, by turn

Aalen–Johansen over leaf-span index: finishing without failing and timing out are ends of their own, and only capped tries are censored; band: bootstrap 95%, resampling inputs, B = 1,000, seed = 0.

| turn | at risk | failed | not yet failed | 95% band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | 15 | 1 | 0.952 | 0.857 – 1.000 |
| 30 | 12 | 1 | 0.905 | 0.714 – 1.000 |
| 33 | 11 | 1 | 0.857 | 0.667 – 1.000 |
| 35 | 10 | 1 | 0.810 | 0.619 – 1.000 |
| 48 | 5 | 1 | 0.762 | 0.571 – 1.000 |
| 50 | 4 | 1 | 0.714 | 0.429 – 1.000 |
| 58 | 2 | 1 | 0.667 | 0.381 – 1.000 |
```

and the kind of step each failed try stopped at:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## Where they die, by kind of step

Aalen–Johansen: each kind's share of tries failed by turn 59, and the share that timed out; band: bootstrap 95%, resampling inputs, B = 1,000, seed = 0.

| kind | tries | share by turn 59 | 95% band |
|---|---|---|---|
| llm | 4 | 0.190 | 0.000 – 0.381 |
| agent | 3 | 0.143 | 0.000 – 0.286 |
| timed out | 0 | 0.000 | 0.000 – 0.000 |
```

`--svg FILE` writes the curve as a picture. Without a `trace.toml`, name the store and the
failures by flag:

<!-- command -->
```
poisson-trace where "cs_agents 2026-09-25 a" --store tests/fixtures/cs \
  --event forbidden_action --event unresolved --event max_turns --event app_error \
  --at 20 --at 40 --svg docs/figures/cs-record.svg --force
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  7 of 24 tries failed; their last steps: 4 at a model call and 3 at an agent step (not necessarily the cause)
  wrote  docs/figures/cs-record.svg
```

[The picture](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/figures/cs-record.svg)
that command writes is in the repository. The recipe
[A first look](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/first-look.md)
goes through these steps one at a time.

### On results in LangSmith, Braintrust or Weave

Results a service holds come in with one `poisson-trace import` for each version. Give the
experiment's address where a file would go, with your key in the environment. Here the two
experiments are a small agent before and after a change, in LangSmith. On this page the two
pulls are answered from LangSmith's own answers, saved with the example files, so the page
runs with no key and no network:

<!-- command pull -->
```
poisson-trace import langsmith langsmith:trace-fixture-baseline-bbb64b8e \
  --store ./experiments --run old --case-from example --outcome-from feedback:exact --cut 0.5 --below
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  wrote run old to ./experiments: 10 rows, 10 cases, 1 repeat each; 6 passed, 4 failed
```

<!-- command pull -->
```
poisson-trace import langsmith langsmith:trace-fixture-candidate-7e3f7200 \
  --store ./experiments --run new --case-from example --outcome-from feedback:exact --cut 0.5 --below
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  wrote run new to ./experiments: 10 rows, 10 cases, 1 repeat each; 8 passed, 2 failed
```

`where` then shows where the old version's failing tries stopped, by step:

<!-- command -->
```
poisson-trace where old --store ./experiments --event missed
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## Share not yet failed, by step

Aalen–Johansen over leaf-span index: finishing without failing and timing out are ends of their own, and only capped tries are censored; band: bootstrap 95%, resampling inputs, B = 1,000, seed = 0.

| step | at risk | failed | not yet failed | 95% band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 10 | 1 | 0.900 | 0.700 – 1.000 |
| 4 | 9 | 3 | 0.600 | 0.300 – 0.900 |
```

and by kind of step:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## Where they die, by kind of step

Aalen–Johansen: each kind's share of tries failed by step 4, and the share that timed out; band: bootstrap 95%, resampling inputs, B = 1,000, seed = 0.

| kind | tries | share by step 4 | 95% band |
|---|---|---|---|
| tool | 1 | 0.100 | 0.000 – 0.300 |
| other | 3 | 0.300 | 0.000 – 0.600 |
| timed out | 0 | 0.000 | 0.000 – 0.000 |
```

and `fix-check` says whether the new version fails less:

<!-- command -->
```
poisson-trace fix-check old new --store ./experiments --event missed \
  --inputs all --max-mde 0.2
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
too small to tell  too few tries to see a drop of any size
```

Four failures down to two, on ten examples run once each, is too few to tell from chance, and
the report says how many repeats would be enough. It also counts each kind of failure in the
two versions, which shows what grew and what shrank:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## Failures by kind

Each failed try's kind of failure, by the built-in rules; the same rules classified both runs. Counts, not a test: the verdict above is about all failures together.

| kind | old | old share | new | new share | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wrong_answer | 3 | 30.0% | 1 | 10.0% | -20.0 points |
| timeout | 1 | 10.0% | 0 | 0.0% | -10.0 points |
| format_error | 0 | 0.0% | 1 | 10.0% | +10.0 points |
| all failures | 4 | 40.0% | 2 | 20.0% | -20.0 points |
```

`where` and `compare` read the steps of each try, so they need a run that carries traces: a
run Prove stored with its traces, or a run imported from LangSmith, Braintrust or Weave by a
pull or from a file of the service's API. The CSV or summary that a service's page downloads
holds no steps, so on a run imported from one `where` says so and `compare` points to
`fix-check`, which needs no traces. The recipes are
[From LangSmith](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-langsmith.md),
[From Braintrust](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-braintrust.md)
and [From Weave](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-weave.md).

## Let your coding agent set it up

`poisson-trace init --agent` writes a skill and a prompt into the two folders coding agents
read skills from, `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`, and nothing else. Trace makes no
model call and reads no key. Give your agent the prompt:

```text
Use the poisson-trace-setup skill in this repository: set Poisson Trace up for me to review, then stop.
```

Your agent reads the repository, runs none of your code, writes `trace.toml`, runs
`poisson-trace doctor --setup` until it passes, and stops. Review what it wrote, then run
`poisson-trace init` yourself: it shows the files the config names and imports them after you
say yes. [Set up Trace with your coding agent](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/setup-with-your-agent.md)
has the steps the agent follows, the check and the hand-over.

## What a fix check says, and what it does not

The usual way to check a fix is to run the failed inputs again on the new version and count
how many now pass. That count has no control: run the old version again on the same inputs,
with nothing changed, and some of them pass too. A fix check puts that number beside the new
version's.

The example is an airline agent, in three runs that Prove stored. The oldest run chose the
inputs: the ones that failed in it. The second is the old version run again, and the newest
is the agent with a guardrail patch:

<!-- command -->
```
mkdir -p airline-agent && cp -R tests/fixtures/tau2 airline-agent/prove-runs
cd airline-agent && poisson-trace init --yes
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  wrote trace.toml: store prove-runs (3 runs), failures unsolved
```

<!-- command -->
```
cd airline-agent && poisson-trace runs
```

<!-- output exit=0 -->
```
ok  3 runs in prove-runs (newest first); 0 named by you, 3 named from their manifests

  #  name                       rows  failed  traces  started           status
  1  tau2-airline 2026-09-17 a    10       3  no      2026-09-17 14:02  complete
  2  tau2-airline 2026-09-15 b   200     112  yes     2026-09-15 21:11  complete
  3  tau2-airline 2026-09-15 a   200     110  yes     2026-09-15 21:01  complete

next: poisson-trace where "tau2-airline 2026-09-15 b"
```

The shortest fix check is the one on the first screen. `--inputs all` compares every input
both runs hold. `--max-mde` is the smallest drop in the share of tries that fail that you
want the check to be able to see, as a fraction: `0.2` is 20 points. Choose it before you
look at a result. Neither has a default.

<!-- command -->
```
cd airline-agent && poisson-trace fix-check previous latest --inputs all --max-mde 0.2
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
too small to tell  too few tries to see a 20-point drop
```

That takes every task the patched run holds. The fix was for the inputs that failed, and
`--failing-from` names the run that chose them, in place of `--inputs all`:

<!-- command -->
```
cd airline-agent && poisson-trace fix-check previous latest \
  --failing-from "tau2-airline 2026-09-15 a" --max-mde 0.20
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
too small to tell  too few tries to see a 20-point drop
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## The control

The old version's run on the inputs that failed in tau2-airline 2026-09-15 a, beside the new.

| version | runs | failed | failure share | did not fail on re-run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| old | 24 | 18 | 75.0% | 25.0% |
| new | 6 | 3 | 50.0% | 50.0% |

Re-running these inputs and counting the runs that did not fail would have read 25.0% on the old version, where nothing changed.
```

Half the tries of the patched version passed, and a quarter of the old version's did too,
with nothing changed. The report then says how small a change these tries could have shown,
and how many repeats of each input would settle the question:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## What it could not have detected

proportional change on every input, 80% power, α = 0.05, continuity-corrected normal approximation to the stratified statistic.

- a drop in failure share: could not have detected one below 64.3 points
- a rise in failure share: no limit; even every run failing, a rise of 30.0 points, would have been detected less than four times in five

**too small to tell: could not have detected a drop in failure share below 64.3 points, and 20 was asked for**

## Guidance

- repeats: 16 per arm on these 6 inputs would bring the limit to 20 points
```

The first line of every fix check is its verdict, one of three:

- *different*: the two runs differ, in the direction the line names. It says the runs differ,
  not why: by itself it does not show that your change caused it.
- *no significant difference*: the gap could be chance, and the tries rule out a change of
  the size you asked about with `--max-mde`. The range of differences the tries fit lies
  inside plus or minus that size. A smaller change may still be there.
- *too small to tell*: the tries cannot rule out a change of the size you asked about. Where
  more tries would settle it, the report says how many.

And every fix check ends with what it cannot say:

- A difference between two runs is a difference between the runs. The version, the provider
  and the hour changed together unless the two were run side by side.
- Repeat tries of one input are read as separate draws, never as replays: nothing matches a
  try of the old version to a try of the new by seed.
- If repeat tries of one input are near copies of one another, the test is more confident
  than it should be. The report's reading by input does not depend on that.
- A try with no outcome is left out of both versions and counted in the header. A new version
  that times out where the old one failed does not show as a failure.
- Trace reads the runs it is given. If the inputs were chosen by the old run's own outcomes,
  or the better of several runs was handed over, the stated confidence does not hold.
- The limit and the number of tries it suggests come from these runs' own failure rates,
  which are estimates. They guide the next run and do not promise its result.

`changes` reads two runs input by input and names the inputs that moved. Here the two runs
are one coding agent run twice, 56 minutes apart, on the same problems, with nothing changed,
saved as two tables of results:

<!-- command -->
```
poisson-trace import table tests/fixtures/ingest/table/humaneval-a.csv \
  --store ./store --run old --case-column case --outcome-column outcome \
  --failed failed_assertion --failed crashed
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  wrote run old to ./store: 10,496 rows, 328 cases, 32 repeats each; 9,158 passed, 1,338 failed
```

<!-- command -->
```
poisson-trace import table tests/fixtures/ingest/table/humaneval-b.csv \
  --store ./store --run new --case-column case --outcome-column outcome \
  --failed failed_assertion --failed crashed
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  wrote run new to ./store: 10,496 rows, 328 cases, 32 repeats each; 9,109 passed, 1,387 failed
```

<!-- command -->
```
poisson-trace changes old new --store ./store --event missed --top 2
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  2 of 328 inputs stand out: case HumanEval/129@0.7 failed more in B; case HumanEval/129@0.0 failed more in B
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
## Inputs that changed

Fisher's exact test per input, Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 over 328 inputs; 2 flagged.

| input | A failed/runs | B failed/runs | change | p | q | flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {"case":"HumanEval/129@0.7"} | 12/32 | 32/32 | +62.5 points | 2.30e-08 | 7.55e-06 | failed more in B |
| {"case":"HumanEval/129@0.0"} | 20/32 | 32/32 | +37.5 points | 1.38e-04 | 0.023 | failed more in B |
```

One problem failed on every try of the second run, and nothing else is flagged. The recipes
are [Check a fix](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/check-a-fix.md)
and [What it cannot say](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/what-it-cannot-say.md).

[Tasks, Prove and Trace together](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/with-tasks-and-prove.md)
runs the three tools end to end with no model: Poisson Tasks makes tasks whose right answer is
known, Prove runs an agent on them before and after a change, and Trace says whether the new
version fails less and at which step the old one stopped.

## The commands

- `poisson-trace init`: set Trace up in a folder, by questions or by flags.
- `poisson-trace runs`: list the runs of a store.
- `poisson-trace name`: give a run a name of yours.
- `poisson-trace where`: where the tries of one run die, by step and by kind of step.
- `poisson-trace compare`: whether tries fail sooner or later in one run than in another.
- `poisson-trace fix-check`: whether a new version fails less than the old, with a control.
- `poisson-trace changes`: which inputs moved between two runs.
- `poisson-trace import`: read in the results another tool wrote, as a run.
- `poisson-trace doctor`: say whether the setup is ready.
- `poisson-trace handover`: check a result written as files.
- `poisson-trace ui`: build pages over a store's runs and saved verdicts.
- `poisson-trace report`: write a result as one HTML page.
- `poisson-trace` on its own: open [the terminal app](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/app.md).

[The commands](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/commands.md) shows the
help of every one, the options they share and the exit codes.
[The config file](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/config.md) goes through
`trace.toml` key by key. The same commands are functions in
[the Python API](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/python.md).

## Results from other tools

Trace reads eleven sources: the runs Prove stored, and the results of ten other tools, which
are DeepEval, Ragas, tables, JUnit, promptfoo, Inspect, OpenAI Evals, LangSmith, Braintrust
and Weave. `poisson-trace import` reads one version's results and writes them as one run, and
every command then reads that run like any other. You say what counts as a failure and what
identifies a case, where the tool's files do not. No prompt and no answer text is kept.

- [DeepEval](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/deepeval.md): its saved test runs, one metric an import. Recipe: [From DeepEval](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-deepeval.md).
- [Ragas](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/ragas.md): a score table you saved, one score an import. Recipe: [From Ragas](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-ragas.md).
- [Tables](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/table.md): any table of results, as CSV, JSON Lines, JSON or Parquet. Recipe: [From a table of results](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-a-table.md).
- [JUnit](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/junit.md): the XML reports pytest and CI systems write. Recipe: [From JUnit reports](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-junit.md).
- [promptfoo](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/promptfoo.md): its results file, one prompt an import. Recipe: [From promptfoo](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-promptfoo.md).
- [Inspect](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/inspect.md): its `.eval` and `.json` logs. Recipe: [From Inspect](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-inspect.md).
- [OpenAI Evals](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/openai-evals.md): the records `oaieval` writes. Recipe: [From OpenAI Evals](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-openai-evals.md).
- [LangSmith](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/langsmith.md): an experiment pulled with your key, or its exported runs. Recipe: [From LangSmith](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-langsmith.md).
- [Braintrust](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/braintrust.md): an experiment pulled with your key, or its exported events. Recipe: [From Braintrust](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-braintrust.md).
- [Weave](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/weave.md): an evaluation pulled with your key, or its exported calls. Recipe: [From Weave](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/from-weave.md).

A tool is listed here only when a real export of it is among the example files committed to
the repository, and its page shows a command run on that file with what Trace printed.

## Into the product

`--out DIR` on `where`, `compare`, `fix-check` or `changes` writes the result as a folder of
files: the result as JSON, the report as text, its table, its charts, and a list of every
file with its digest. `poisson-trace handover --check DIR` holds such a folder to that list
before your code reads it. [The handover](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/handover.md)
says what each file holds and which keys are promised, and the recipe is
[Into the product](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/into-the-product.md).

**The pages.** `poisson-trace report DIR` turns that folder into one HTML page that opens from
disk with nothing else present, to send to someone who does not have Trace: the recipe is
[A page to send](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/recipes/a-page-to-send.md).
`poisson-trace ui` builds pages over a whole store, its runs and every saved verdict. Neither
loads anything from the network.

## How it decides

Every verdict comes from a named statistical test with a stated level, chosen for small
numbers of tries: exact tests where they exist, and resampling for the bands. A fix check
compares the two versions inside each input, so an input that is hard for both does not
count against either. Each report prints the test it used, the level, and the smallest change
the tries could have shown.

[How it decides](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/how-it-decides.md)
names each test, says how the three verdicts are chosen, and lists the flags that set a size,
a level or a seed. The test suite holds every one of them against an independent reference.

## What is built and what is not claimed

Trace reads stored results. It does not run your agent, record its calls or change its code,
and nothing it reads leaves your machine.

A verdict is about the two runs you gave it, not about the two versions: whatever else
differed between the runs is part of the difference. Looking after every few tries and
stopping when the verdict reads well is not covered by the stated confidence, and no report
can see it. `compare` does not pair tries by seed, even when two runs share their seeds.
The example files hold one pair that reads *different* with fewer failures: a base model and
its fine-tuned version, scored by Ragas, on two of its three scores, which
[the Ragas page](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/docs/integrations/ragas.md)
shows. The pairs on this page read *too small to tell*, or *different* where nothing was
changed, and the page says why each time.

## Development

working copy, the test lanes, the docs check and the rules a change is held to.
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) says what each

# Set up Trace with your coding agent

You have results already: the runs Poisson Prove recorded of your agent, or the files your
evaluation tools wrote. Setting Trace up means telling it where those results are, which
outcomes count as a failure, which files to import and what each is, and which results come
from before a change and which from after. `poisson-trace init` asks you those questions.
`poisson-trace init --agent` hands them to your own coding agent instead: it writes a skill
and a prompt into your repository, your agent reads the repository and writes `trace.toml`,
runs Trace's check until it passes, and stops for you to review. Trace makes no model call
and reads no key; your agent does the work, with the model and the key it already has.

## What `init --agent` writes

Four files, in the two folders coding agents read skills from, and nothing else:

| folder | read by | files |
|---|---|---|
| `.agents/skills/` | Codex, Cursor | `poisson-trace-setup/SKILL.md`, `poisson-trace-setup/prompt.txt` |
| `.claude/skills/` | Claude Code, Cursor | the same two files, byte for byte |

`SKILL.md` is the setup file in the Poisson setup-file format (version 1): an Agent Skills
skill with the steps, the rules and the check. `prompt.txt` holds the one line you give your
agent. Trace never writes `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, a rules file or anything else you own; a
file of the four that is there already is refused unless you give `--force`, which replaces
those four alone. `--repo DIR` writes into another folder; `--print` prints the skill and
writes nothing.

Here it is in a small repository made from the example files of a clone of Trace's repository:
a Prove store, two Ragas score tables and two JUnit reports.

<!-- command -->
```
mkdir -p my-repo/evals/results my-repo/reports
cp -R tests/fixtures/cs my-repo/store
cp tests/fixtures/ingest/ragas/rag-base.jsonl tests/fixtures/ingest/ragas/rag-raft.jsonl my-repo/evals/results/
cp tests/fixtures/ingest/junit/humaneval-a.xml my-repo/reports/junit-old.xml
cp tests/fixtures/ingest/junit/humaneval-b.xml my-repo/reports/junit-new.xml
cd my-repo && poisson-trace init --agent
```

<!-- output exit=0 -->
```
ok  wrote the setup for your coding agent (4 files)
  wrote  .agents/skills/poisson-trace-setup/SKILL.md
  wrote  .agents/skills/poisson-trace-setup/prompt.txt
  wrote  .claude/skills/poisson-trace-setup/SKILL.md
  wrote  .claude/skills/poisson-trace-setup/prompt.txt
  prompt  Use the poisson-trace-setup skill in this repository: set Poisson Trace up for me to review, then stop.
  next: give your coding agent the prompt above, then review what it wrote
```

## The prompt

Give your agent this line, in the repository the files were written into:

```text
Use the poisson-trace-setup skill in this repository: set Poisson Trace up for me to review, then stop.
```

## What the agent does

The skill tells the agent to read and run nothing, in seven steps: find the results on disk
(Prove stores, and every file a reader in the install reads: DeepEval's saved test runs, Ragas
tables, tables of results, JUnit reports, promptfoo results, Inspect logs, OpenAI Evals records,
and LangSmith, Braintrust and Weave exports; the readers are `deepeval`, `ragas`, `table`,
`junit`, `promptfoo`, `inspect`, `openai-evals`, `langsmith`, `braintrust` and `weave`); work out which tool wrote each from the repository's dependencies and the
tools' own configuration; find the outcomes that count as a failure, and for a scored file the
metric and the cut, in the code that scores (the agent never chooses a cut: a file whose cut
the code does not name is left out, and the hand-over says so); work out which results are old
and which new; write `trace.toml` with `[store]`, `[events]`, one `[[import]]` table per file
and `[names]`, and nothing else; run the check; stop and hand over.

The rules it follows: it runs no `poisson-trace` command but the check and `--help`, passes
no `--yes`, reads no key and no `.env` file, installs nothing, writes into no store, and never
runs your evaluations, tests or agent to make results.

## The check

The agent runs `poisson-trace doctor --setup` until it passes, at most three fixes. It reads
what `doctor` reads and each `[[import]]` file not imported yet, with its reader, and writes
nothing.

No agent runs on this page, so the `trace.toml` an agent would write for the small repository
is copied in from the example files. This is the file:

<!-- command -->
```
cp tests/fixtures/setup-agent/expected/trace.toml my-repo/trace.toml
cat my-repo/trace.toml
```

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
[store]
path = "store"

[events]
failed = ["forbidden_action", "unresolved", "max_turns", "app_error"]

[[import]]
file = "evals/results/rag-base.jsonl"
tool = "ragas"
name = "rag-base"
metric = "faithfulness"
cut = 0.5
below = true
case_column = "case"
```

And the check on it:

<!-- command -->
```
cd my-repo && poisson-trace doctor --setup
```

Ready is exit 0. The first line is the verdict:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  trace.toml is ready for the person to review
```

Under it come two lines that name your Python and where the package is installed, and then
one line for each thing checked, with one line per pending file:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
  prove     poisson-prove 0.1.3 (the version Trace reads)
  config    trace.toml: store store (2 runs, 2 complete, 0 partial), failures forbidden_action, unresolved, max_turns, app_error
  names     store: no names of yours yet
  readers   deepeval, ragas, table, junit, promptfoo, inspect, openai-evals, langsmith, braintrust, weave
  import    evals/results/rag-base.jsonl: ragas, 150 rows, faithfulness at 0.5, not imported yet
  import    evals/results/rag-raft.jsonl: ragas, 150 rows, faithfulness at 0.5, not imported yet
  import    reports/junit-old.xml: junit, 656 rows, not imported yet
  import    reports/junit-new.xml: junit, 656 rows, not imported yet
next: poisson-trace init
```

Not ready is exit 1, with `error:` naming the first failing check and a `next:` line for
each; a setting wrong under `trace.toml`'s rules (an unknown key, a tool not in the install,
a name used twice, a required option missing) is exit 2 with the line it is on.

## The hand-over, and what you do next

The agent stops and tells you what it wrote, the check's last output, and what you must
confirm: the stores and files it found and those it left out, the failure outcomes and where
in the code each came from, the metric and cut per scored file, and which run is old and
which new. Then you run `poisson-trace init` yourself, on a terminal. Here the question is
answered `y`:

<!-- command tty answers="y" -->
```
cd my-repo && poisson-trace init
```

It shows what the config names, on stderr, and asks:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
  store store: 2 runs
  failures: forbidden_action, unresolved, max_turns, app_error
  files to import:
    evals/results/rag-base.jsonl  as the run rag-base (ragas)
    evals/results/rag-raft.jsonl  as the run rag-raft (ragas)
    reports/junit-old.xml  as the run tests-old (junit)
    reports/junit-new.xml  as the run tests-new (junit)
```

and on a yes it imports them and says what it did, on stdout:

<!-- excerpt exit=0 -->
```
ok  imported 4 runs into trace-store, failures forbidden_action, unresolved, max_turns, app_error; [store.imported] added to trace.toml
  prove    poisson-prove is installed at the version Trace reads
  import   poisson-trace import ragas evals/results/rag-base.jsonl --store trace-store --run rag-base --metric faithfulness --cut 0.5 --below --case-column case
  import   poisson-trace import ragas evals/results/rag-raft.jsonl --store trace-store --run rag-raft --metric faithfulness --cut 0.5 --below --case-column case
  import   poisson-trace import junit reports/junit-old.xml --store trace-store --run tests-old --case name
  import   poisson-trace import junit reports/junit-new.xml --store trace-store --run tests-new --case name
  the same setup, without questions:
    poisson-trace init --yes --import
next: poisson-trace doctor
```

On a `trace.toml` with `[[import]]` files not imported yet, `init` shows the stores, the
failures and the files, and asks `Import these 4 files as the runs named here? [y/N]`. On a
yes it imports them into `trace-store` beside `trace.toml` (or the store the config names for
them), writes `trace.toml` once more keeping every line the agent wrote and adding the store's
table, and ends with `next: poisson-trace doctor`; `doctor` then reads ready, and its next
command is the first fix-check on the first pair of one tool's runs. `--yes` or `--import`
answers yes without the question; `--no-import` leaves the files pending.

## `[[import]]`

One table per file to import, with the reader's options by their flags' names without the
dashes:

```toml
[[import]]
file = "evals/results/rag-base.jsonl"   # relative to trace.toml, inside the repository
tool = "ragas"                          # a reader in the install
name = "rag-base"                       # the run's name
metric = "faithfulness"                 # the reader's own options, by their flag names
cut = 0.5
below = true
case_column = "case"
```

Every command that reads `trace.toml` checks the keys, the types and the choices; only
`doctor --setup` and `init` open the files. A `[signals]` table's `case_field`,
`outcome_field`, `score_field` and `cut` stand in for an entry's `case_column`,
`outcome_column`, `metric` or `score_column`, and `cut` where the entry leaves them out, as
they do for `poisson-trace import`'s flags.

## What it does not do

It does not call a model, read a key or contact a host. It does not run your evaluations or
your tests. It does not choose a cut. It does not import anything: the import is yours, after
the review.

name = "poisson-trace"
version = "0.1.0a1"
description = "Where in the workflow an agent's runs die, and whether a change made them fail less: read from the results you already have in Prove, LangSmith, Braintrust, Weave and seven other tools."
readme = "README.md"
license = { file = "LICENSE" }
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
authors = [{ name = "Poisson Labs", email = "work@poissonlabs.ai" }]
maintainers = [{ name = "Poisson Labs", email = "work@poissonlabs.ai" }]
keywords = ["survival-analysis", "kaplan-meier", "agents", "evaluation", "traces"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
# Prove (the `poisson-prove` package, imported as `poisson_prove`) is the one thing Trace reads
# stored runs through, so it is pinned exactly: Prove changes fast, and an exact pin keeps Trace
# steady until the pin is moved on purpose. This is the one place the version is written;
# `poisson_trace.look` reads it back from the installed package's metadata, so the version Trace
# checks for, the refusal's install command and this line cannot drift apart.
# Rich draws the pretty rendering on a terminal (docs/cli-look.md, rule 16) and is imported by
# poisson_trace/_pretty.py and the terminal app's modules alone; the floor is the one Prove
# declares. Textual is the terminal app's framework (spec section 17.2, AD5), imported by
# poisson_trace/_app*.py alone, at the floor Prove declares.
dependencies = ["numpy", "scipy", "pandas>=2", "pyarrow>=17.0.0", "poisson-prove==0.1.3", "rich>=14.2.0", "textual>=6.4.0"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# pyte reads a pseudo-terminal's screen back for the clean-look tests
# zstandard reads an Inspect .eval log, whose members are Zstandard-compressed
inspect = ["zstandard>=0.22"]
dev = ["pytest", "pytest-xdist", "hypothesis", "mypy", "ruff", "lifelines", "pyte", "zstandard>=0.22", "poisson-tasks==0.4.2"]

[project.scripts]
poisson-trace = "poisson_trace.cli:main"
poisson-trace-import = "poisson_trace.ingest.cli:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace"
Repository = "https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace"
Issues = "https://github.com/poisson-labs/trace/issues"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/poisson_trace"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# the repository's own working rules, and (with hatch_build.py) its ignore file, are not part of
# the source a user gets; nor is test_tf10_fixtures.py, which holds a path from the machine its
# fixtures were made on (ruled 2026-11-11, the 0.1.0a1 cut; the path itself is owed to 0.1.0)
exclude = ["docs/repo-hygiene.md", "/.gitignore", "/tests/test_tf10_fixtures.py"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.hooks.custom]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "B"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["I", "E501", "E702", "B905"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
files = ["src"]
strict = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["pandas", "pandas.*", "pyarrow", "pyarrow.*", "scipy", "scipy.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# The lanes, named as Prove's are (spec section 17.5):
#   code, on every pull request:  python -m pytest -n 10 -m "not math and not lane_j and not slow" tests
#   math, the statistics:         python -m pytest -n 10 -m math tests
#   slow, the rest:               python -m pytest -n 10 -m slow tests
#   lane_j, the real tools:       python -m pytest -m lane_j tests
# A -m given on the command line replaces the one below, so the code lane names lane_j itself.
# Lane J holds every test that reads PyPI: DeepEval and Ragas run themselves, and the Trace wheel
# installed into a clean environment, which must bring the one Prove it declares. On every pull
# request the code lane checks that declaration instead, against the Prove installed.
# Each lane, `ruff check src tests` and `mypy --strict` run on two Pythons: 3.11, the oldest this
# declares, and a current one (3.12.13 or later). Python 3.12 changed how builtin sum() adds
# floats and 3.12.7 how argparse lays out a help page, so an output pinned on one is checked on
# the other before a release and on a pull request that changes how a number or a help is made.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = ["-m", "not lane_j"]
markers = [
    "lane_j: reads PyPI: runs another tool itself (DeepEval, Ragas) at its pinned version, or installs the Trace wheel into a clean environment; deselected unless -m lane_j",
    "slow: a test that runs every invocation of a corpus where the pull-request lane keeps a fast test of the same invariant on a few (the clean look over the whole conformance corpus; a statistics scenario at the check's seeds; a wide Hypothesis property check, test_hy_*.py); nightly and before every release",
    "math: the math suite, a statistic's slow property checks against its reference where the pull-request lane keeps a fast test of the same invariant; runs on a pull request that changes the statistics code (src/poisson_trace/paired.py, survival.py), a test of the math suite, or the resolved numpy, scipy, pandas or lifelines, nightly and before every release",
]
